> 第一章寒世孤存（第1页）
隆冬腊月，大雪封了整座青阳城周边的山林。
山间小道被厚雪覆盖，踩上去咯吱作响，寒风卷着雪粒，打在脸上生疼。陈默背着半篓刚采摘的普通草药，缩着脖子快步前行。
他今年十六，彻头彻尾的凡人，无父无母，靠着在山林采药、换些粗粮勉强度日，连修士的门槛都未曾踏足。
青阳城一带修仙风气盛行，城内有林家修士家族，往来也多是修行之人。可仙路高高在上，对寻常凡人而言，那是遥不可及的云端之事。陈默从小便清楚，自己和那些飞天遁地的修士，本就是两个世界的人。
山路偏僻，荒无人烟，唯有风声在林间回荡。他怀里揣着一团温热，是一只巴掌大的小白狐，他唤作小雪。去年寒冬，他在雪地里捡到了这只奄奄一息的小狐狸。小雪并非什么灵狐异种，只是山野间最普通的狐狸，身子天生孱弱，畏寒怕冷，平日里连跑动都没什么力气。这一路风雪太大，陈默便把它揣在怀中保暖。
回到自己栖身的破败山屋，屋子是早年猎户遗留下来的，土墙斑驳，屋顶漏风，四处都透着寒气。屋内没有炭火，只有一张破旧木床、一张矮桌，家徒四壁。
陈默将药篓放在墙角，小心翼翼把小雪放到铺着干茅草的窝里。小家伙抖了抖雪白的绒毛，睁着懵懂的眼睛看他，细弱地叫了两声。
他拿出一点粗粮碎粒，放在木碟里。这便是他和小雪一天的吃食，寡淡无味，却已是当下能找到的最好食物。
这些年，他靠着采草药换铜钱，勉强糊口。可寻常草药价值低微，遇上大雪封山，山路难行，往往几日都换不来多少吃食。日子过得拮据又清苦，时时刻刻都要为温饱发愁。
偶尔会有林家外院的弟子进山历练、采摘灵草。那些人身着整洁衣袍，步履轻盈，周身隐隐有异样气息流转，与满身尘土、手脚粗糙的陈默对比鲜明。旁人路过，大多目光淡漠，甚至带着几分轻视。在修士眼中，挣扎求生的凡人，和山野走兽并无太大区别。
也曾有人随口提过引气修行之事，说凡人若能引天地灵气入体，便可脱凡胎、寿元大增。可陈默连最基础的入门法门都接触不到，更别提灵石、丹药这些修行所需之物。仙路二字，于他而言，只是听过的传说。
山屋内寒意刺骨，陈默裹紧单薄的旧衣，靠在墙角闭目歇息。腹中饥饿，身上冻得发麻，一日的劳累翻涌上来，满心皆是无力。
他只是个最底层的凡人，守着一间破屋，伴着一只弱狐，在寒冬山野里，只求活下去而已。很快，他便慢慢的睡在了破了几个洞的草席上。那头狐狸也慢慢的偷偷的躲进了他的怀里。梦中，他看到了金钱，名利自己也成了一位大修士。艰难的生活与他相去甚远。一切的美都在梦中重现。

>Chapter 1: Alone in the Cold World (Page 1)
In the twelfth lunar month of winter, heavy snow sealed the entire mountain forest around Qingyang City.
The mountain trails were covered with thick snow and creaked when you stepped on them. The cold wind carried the snow particles and hit your face painfully. Chen Mo carried half a basket of freshly picked common herbs on his back, hunched his neck and walked quickly.
He is sixteen years old, a complete mortal, without a father or a mother. He makes a living by collecting herbs in the mountains and forests and exchanging some coarse grains. He has never even set foot on the threshold of a monk.
The practice of cultivating immortals is prevalent in Qingyang City. There are Lin family monks in the city, and there are many people who come and go as cultivators. But the Immortal Road is high above, and for ordinary mortals, it is something out of reach in the clouds. Chen Mo has known since he was a child that he and the monks who flew to the sky and escaped from the earth are originally from two different worlds.
The mountain road is remote and deserted, with only the sound of wind echoing in the forest. In his arms was a warm ball, a small white fox as big as a palm, which he called Xiaoxue. Last winter, he picked up this dying little fox in the snow. Xiaoxue is not a strange spirit fox, but the most common fox in the mountains. Her body is naturally weak and afraid of the cold. She doesn't even have the strength to run on weekdays. There was too much wind and snow along the way, so Chen Mo put it in his arms to keep warm.
Returning to the dilapidated mountain house where he lived, the house was left behind by hunters in the early years. The earthen walls were mottled, the roof was leaking, and there was a cold air everywhere. There was no charcoal fire in the house, only a dilapidated wooden bed, a low table, and only four walls.
Chen Mo placed the medicine basket in the corner and carefully placed Xiaoxue into the nest covered with dry thatch. The little guy shook his snow-white fur, looked at him with ignorant eyes, and called twice weakly.
He took out some grain crumbs and put them on a wooden plate. This is what he and Xiaoxue eat for a day. It is tasteless, but it is the best food they can find at the moment.
Over the years, he scraped by collecting herbs in exchange for copper coins. However, the value of ordinary medicinal herbs is low. When the mountains are blocked by heavy snow and the mountain roads are difficult to travel, they often cannot get much food in exchange for several days. Life was tight and miserable, and I had to worry about food and clothing all the time.
Occasionally, disciples from the Lin family's outer courtyard would go into the mountains to practice and pick spiritual herbs. Those people were dressed in neat robes, walking lightly, and there was a faint strange aura circulating around them, which was in stark contrast to Chen Mo, who was covered in dust and had rough hands and feet. Most of the people passing by looked at him indifferently, even with a bit of contempt. In the eyes of monks, mortals struggling to survive are not much different from wild beasts.
Someone once casually mentioned the practice of entraining qi, saying that if mortals could induce the spiritual qi of heaven and earth into their bodies, they would be able to escape from the mortal world and their life span would be greatly increased. But Chen Mo didn't even have access to the most basic entry-level techniques, let alone spiritual stones and elixirs that were needed for practice. To him, the word "immortal road" is just a legend he has heard.
It was bitingly cold in the mountain house. Chen Mo wrapped up his thin old clothes tightly and leaned against the corner with his eyes closed to rest. I was hungry in my belly, my body was numb from the cold, the fatigue of the day was pouring over me, and my heart was full of weakness.
He is just a mortal at the lowest level, guarding a shabby house with a weak fox, just trying to survive in the cold winter mountains. Soon, he slowly fell asleep on the straw mat with a few holes in it. The fox also slowly and secretly hid in his arms. In the dream, he saw money, fame and fortune, and he became a great monk. A hard life was far away from him. All the beauty reappears in the dream.
